newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU calls for immediate release of Burma detainees.
newsitem.headline: EU calls for immediate release of Burma detainees.

text.p: The European Union on Tuesday called for the immediate release of more than 500 people detained by Burmese military rulers in a crackdown on pro-democracy activity.

The General Affairs Council released a statement saying it was very concerned at the situation in Burma and calling on the State Law and Order Restoration Committee (SLORC) to lift a blockade on the home of opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

Burma's military government said on Tuesday it had released 88 of the 559 supporters of the National League for Democracy (NLD) party held since Thursday, but roadblocks around her house remained in place.
Senior officials had said the activists were only being held temporarily to prevent unrest and would be released soon.

The government says the party meeting aimed to incite instability and rioting. The NLD says it was to celebrate the eighth anniversary of the founding of the party, born in 1988 after unprecedented protests against years of military rule.
Officials also claimed Suu Kyi had been trying to cause unrest and confrontation with the government since she was released from six years of house arrest in July 1995.

"The European Union wishes to emphasise the need for a genuine dialogue to commence without delay between SLORC and the NDL as being the only possible credible way forward for national reconciliation," the Council statement said.
